summary.title: The Secret to a Great Planning Process — Lessons from Airbnb and Eventbrite
summary.one_liner: A four-step "W Framework" (Context, Plans, Integration, Buy-in) for running company-wide annual and quarterly planning with clear roles between leadership and teams.
keywords: leadership and team roles in planning
how to run a planning cycle
takeaways: Planning works best with top-down context from leadership plus bottom-up proposals from teams, not either extreme alone.
Use four steps: Leadership provides context, Teams respond with proposed plans, Leadership integrates a single plan, and Teams confirm buy-in.
Define who is responsible for what and when, including timelines, owners, accountability and the final decision-maker.
Focus resources on a small number of bets (ideally 3, max 5) and watch for common pitfalls like working in silos or doing too much.
Leadership should share a company strategy with mission, vision, goal, strategy and strategic pillars, and be explicit about what it does not yet know.
summary.summary: The article by Lenny Rachitsky and Nels Gilbreth, drawing on their time at Airbnb and Eventbrite, lays out a "W Framework" for company planning aimed at organizations larger than roughly 25 people. It defines the roles of the Leadership group (set vision, goal, and final prioritization) and the Teams (develop execution plans and commit to goals with resources). Each of the four steps is walked through with best practices, templates referenced by the authors, and common pitfalls. The piece is practical and example-driven, with sections on strategy documents, team planning workflows, and integrating plans by prioritizing and allocating resources.
